interface.title: LigandNexus (v0.2.5)
interface.field: Computational coordination chemistry / chemoinformatics (metal–ligand and metal–polyphenol complexes)
interface.stage_of_work: Pre-computation: picking candidates, analysing donor and chelation sites, and building starting geometries plus input files for DFT
interface.what_it_is_for: Find where a ligand or polyphenol can bind a metal, estimate which Fe/Cu–polyphenol species dominates at a given pH, and build 3D complex or ligand geometries with Gaussian/ORCA/Psi4 input files ready for DFT.

data.note: Used the built-in 'Prueba rápida' polyphenol list (gallic acid CID 370, quercetin, ellagic acid; all loaded offline) and typed SMILES: caffeic acid, a made-up N/O/S/P ligand, and 2,2'-bipyridine. Every PubChem CID or name lookup (Átomos coordinantes, Cribado general) hung with no error, because the server has no network. Leaving a page reset that page's state.

screens_never_reached: Cribado general steps after '1 · Molécula base' (database choice, derivative retrieval, range filtering, CSV/Excel export): Verificar with CID 1474 and with CID 370 hung with no error because PubChem is unreachable (screens/055.webp, screens/061.webp, screens/062.webp)

Análisis de coordinación tabs ② Depurar, ③ Clasificar, ④ Seleccionar, 💊 ADMET, ⑤ Exportar: the ADMET tab says 'Complete al menos el paso ① para poder perfilar las moléculas', and step ① needs a PubChem CID or name lookup (screens/057.webp, screens/058.webp)
Geometrías 3D 'Un conjunto del cribado' batch mode: selecting it shows 'No hay conjuntos cargados' because no screening set could be made offline (screens/043.webp)
Uploading an SDF/SMILES/CSV file as the derivative source: no test files were available and the upload step sits behind the Cribado lookup
not_done: Derivative screening, the tool's headline purpose: retrieving a base molecule's derivatives from PubChem, ChEMBL, COCONUT or a downloaded dump (or an uploaded file), then filtering them by property ranges and exporting to CSV/Excel. Needs network access; the Cribado general lookup hung (screens/055.webp, screens/061.webp, screens/062.webp).

Coordination-analysis pipeline (clean the set, classify substituents, pick a representative donor/acceptor-balanced set): every tab after ① needs step ① to finish, which needs a PubChem lookup (screens/057.webp).

ADMET / drug-likeness goal (Lipinski, Veber, Egan, logBB, QED, PAINS): could not be reached. It sits only in the Análisis de coordinación ADMET tab, which needs a PubChem lookup in step ① first, and that lookup cannot finish offline (screens/058.webp).

The CID and Nombre input modes in Átomos coordinantes, Geometrías 3D and the polyphenol 'buscar otra molécula' box: typing CID 1474 in Átomos coordinantes and pressing Analizar hung with no result (screens/033.webp, screens/035.webp); only SMILES works offline.

Reading the ORCA and Psi4 outputs: they downloaded as orca.zip and psi4.zip, which the download reader shows only as binary sizes, so the generated .inp/.in contents (and whether the 'B3LYP D3BJ' template edit reached them) were not checked. The Gaussian .gjf for the Cu(II)–quercetin complex and the manifest CSV were read.

Spin-multiplicity bug: the Multiplicidad de espín default does not follow the metal, because views/hierro.py:225 creates the widget with a fixed key='fe_mult', so Streamlit keeps the default of the first metal chosen in the session. As a result the exported Cu(II)–quercetin .gjf has the header '-2 6', which is wrong: Cu(II) is d9 and should be a doublet ('-2 2'). Fe(II) also showed 6 and was set to 5 by hand (screens/019.webp, screens/065.webp, screens/067.webp).

In Geometrías 3D, 'Mejor energía (varios)' with 10 conformers still reported conformeros = 1 in the manifest (screens/052.webp). It is unclear whether that counts the conformer kept or means only one was searched.
Tannic acid (galotannin) was not tried in polynuclear mode; ellagic acid was used instead to keep the build fast.
